newsitem.title: CANADA: Domtar still seeks merger with Avenor/Repap.
newsitem.headline: Domtar still seeks merger with Avenor/Repap.

text.p: Domtar Inc said on Wednesday that it was still interested in pursuing a three-way merger with Avenor Inc and Repap Enterprises Inc.
"We were and we remain interested in putting the three companies together. We still think it is a good idea," Domtar spokesman Denis Couture told Reuters.

Couture said Domtar was reviewing its options after Avenor shareholders today rejected Avenor's proposed C$2.6 billion merger with Repap. Couture said no talks were under way among the three companies.

He said Domtar's position was the same -- that a merger between Domtar, which significantly lowered its debt in recent years and sold non-core assets in newsprint -- and Avenor and Repap, would create a competitive and well-capitalized forest products company.
Domtar is Canada's largest producer of fine papers. Repap is the country's biggest maker of coated papers and Avenor is a major producer of newsprint, pulp and white paper.
"If it is at all possible to do, we would be very pleased to put the deal together," Couture said.
But Couture said a three-way merger would be more difficult to achieve after the shareholder rejection of the Avenor/Repap merger.
"We knew all along that if it was a no, it would be much more difficult because there is no legal link between Repap and Avenor any more," he said.
